source.title: On three open problems related to quasi relative interior

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separated locally convex space. For a convex set C ⊂ X, define its quasi relative interior by qri(C) = {x ∈ C | cone(C − x) is a linear space}. Given convex sets C, D ⊂ X, must the inclusion qri(C) + qri(D) ⊆ qri(C + D) be strict for some choice of C and D; equivalently, do there exist convex sets C and D for which qri(C) + qri(D) is a proper subset of qri(C + D)?
accepted.context_brief: Properness of qri under Minkowski addition

evidence.quote: Borwein and Goebel, in [1, p. 2548], say “Can qri C+qri D be a proper subset of qri(C+D)? (Almost certainly such sets do exist.)”
The next example answers to both problems mentioned above.
Clearly C and D are convex sets, qri C = icr C = (0, 1)x, qri D = qi D = { (xn)n≥1 ⊂ ℓ1 | xn > 0 ∀n ≥ 1 } and x ∈ qi(C + D) = qri(C + D), but x /∈ C + qi D ⊃ qri C + qri D.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separated locally convex space, let A, B ⊂ X be convex sets, and define the quasi interior of a convex set E by qi(E) = {x ∈ E | cone(E − x) = X}. Assuming qi(B) is nonempty, is it always true that A + qi(B) = qi(A + B)?
accepted.context_brief: Equality involving quasi interior and sum

evidence.quote: while Grad and Pop, in [5, p. 26], say: “we conjecture that in general when A, B ⊆ V are convex sets with qi B 6= ∅, it holds A + qi B = qi(A + B)”.
The next example answers to both problems mentioned above.
Clearly C and D are convex sets, qri C = icr C = (0, 1)x, qri D = qi D = { (xn)n≥1 ⊂ ℓ1 | xn > 0 ∀n ≥ 1 } and x ∈ qi(C + D) = qri(C + D), but x /∈ C + qi D ⊃ qri C + qri D.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a separated locally convex space. For a convex set C ⊂ X, define its quasi relative interior by qri(C) = {x ∈ C | cone(C − x) is a linear space}. Given nonempty convex sets C, D ⊂ X such that qri(C) ∩ qri(D) is nonempty, can the inclusion qri(C ∩ D) ⊂ qri(C) ∩ qri(D) fail?

evidence.quote: Borwein and Goebel, in [1, p. 2548], also say “Can qri(C ∩ D) ⊂ qri C ∩ qri D fail when qri C ∩ qri D 6= ∅?” Proposition 3 (ii) shows that the answer to this question is negative.
(ii) If qri C ∩ qri D 6= ∅ then qri(C ∩ D) ⊂ qri C ∩ qri D.
